chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Sa'id, from al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever wears clothes that make him notorious, God will clothe him on the Day of Resurrection in a garment from the Fire.

key_terms.ثَوْبٌ مِنَ النَّارِ: A garment from the Fire — eschatological punishment mirroring worldly sin
key_terms.يَشْهَرُهُ: Makes him notorious/famous — shuhra refers to conspicuousness or seeking public attention through appearance

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about wearing clothes for fame or showing off?
ai.summary: Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) warns against wearing clothing for the purpose of showing off or gaining notoriety — commonly called 'clothes of fame' (thiyab al-shuhra). The hadith employs the principle of divine retribution in kind: just as one sought attention through conspicuous dress in this world, God will dress him in garments of fire in the next. This teaching reflects early Islamic ethics on humility in dress and the prohibition of vanity (kibr) and ostentation (riya').
